defects: The hypothesis hbv requires bounded variation over ALL partitions with points in the interval Icc a b (unrestricted to s), rather than partitions restricted to s ∩ neighborhood as in mathlib's LocallyBoundedVariationOn f s — this is a strictly stronger (non-equivalent) hypothesis than the gold's, since it bounds variation over a superset of partitions.

The conclusion completely omits the 'moreover' clause of the informal statement: the requirement that the combined increments of the two monotone parts equal the total variation (gold's ∀ x y ∈ s, (p y - p x) + (q y - q x) = variationOnFromTo f s x y) is missing entirely.

Conclusion uses global Monotone g / Monotone h (monotonicity over all of ℝ) instead of MonotoneOn p s / MonotoneOn q s (monotonicity only on s), changing the structure and strength of the claim relative to gold.
f = p - q in gold is a global function equality, while the produced statement only asserts equality pointwise on s (∀ x ∈ s, f x = g x - h x) — a weaker version of that conjunct.

The partition-based definition of bounded variation does not require a and b to be endpoints of the list p nor enforce a minimum length, making the encoded notion of variation only loosely correspond to the standard definition used in LocallyBoundedVariationOn.
